def: Splitting the rows into k folds, training on k minus 1 of them and scoring on the held-out one in turn, then averaging the k scores.
One of the k parts of the data in cross-validation, used once for validation and k minus 1 times for training.
A k-fold split that deals each class out separately so every fold has nearly the same class proportions.
A k-fold split that keeps all rows of one group, such as a patient or customer, in the same fold so no group appears on both sides.
A time-respecting split in which each fold trains on everything before a cut-off and validates on the block just after it.
A time-based split that trains on a fixed-length recent stretch of the past instead of all of it.
Rows dropped between the training window and the validation block so that labels or features that overlap the cut-off cannot leak.
The extreme of k-fold where k equals the number of rows, so each row is validated by a model trained on all the others.
Running k-fold several times with different shuffles and pooling the scores to reduce the luck of one partition.
An outer loop that holds out data and an inner loop that does all model selection on the rest, so the outer score is not flattered by the selection.
The optimism in the best of many noisy validation scores, caused by choosing the winner on the same rows used to score it.
